name: Fertiliser supply
summary: US urea $657 a tonne in mid-November, below its spring peak; Egyptian supply cut and Hormuz threats keep Watch
state: US retail urea averaged $657 a tonne in the week of 9–13 Nov, slightly below mid-October and well under the $866 peak of late April, though 10% higher than a year earlier (DTN, 18 Nov). Egyptian granular urea export prices reached $535 a tonne after gas deliveries to producers were cut from 1 Nov, about 17% above September (UkrAgroConsult). DTN cites threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which carries Gulf nitrogen exports; searches on 28 Nov found no urea rise above 30% in three months and no export bans by several major exporters.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen for spring planting face prices above last year's; higher fertiliser costs tend to feed into crop prices in the following season. Gulf-dependent importers in South Asia and Africa are most exposed to Hormuz disruption.
rubric_hit: Impeded Gulf export route via Hormuz and Egyptian supply cut: Watch; urea below +60% in three months for Alert

sources.title: DTN — Retail fertilizer trends: major fertilizer prices edge mixed
UkrAgroConsult — Egyptian urea prices rise to $535 per ton amid gas supply restrictions

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
